findings.title: Late intimation to insurer
findings.explanation_en: Intimated 60h after admission vs 24h in policy. Delay alone should not defeat a genuine claim.

explanations.en: Intimated 60h after admission vs 24h in policy. Delay alone should not defeat a genuine claim.

findings.fix: Ask the treating surgeon / Medical Superintendent for a 2-line emergency certificate: 'Patient admitted in emergency and taken straight for emergency surgery on [date/time], attendant could not intimate earlier.' Attach OT notes + discharge summary showing 'emergency admission'. Write to insurer Grievance Cell: 'Condone 60-hour delay per IRDAI Standardization Guidelines - delay was beyond our control due to emergency surgery, claim is otherwise genuine - please reconsider.' If denied, escalate to Ombudsman.

irdai_cite.doc: IRDAI standard terms and conditions (Standardization Guidelines 2020) [IN-CONDONE-DELAY]
irdai_cite.quote: Claims should not be rejected solely for delayed intimation or document submission where the delay is for reasons beyond the insured's control.

tool_evidence.advocate_argument: Policy clause 5.1 requires 24h intimation, but 60h delay was due to emergency surgery which is beyond insured's control. Regulator rule IN-CONDONE-DELAY overrides policy and bars rejection solely for delayed intimation in such cases. Reimbursement claim with genuine emergency is condonable.
